title: Culture and Heritages in India-I: Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Name the place and the person. (a) Name the sacred site situated at the tip of the Indian peninsula. (b) Name the last Tirthankara of the Jains.
questions.answer: (a) Rameshwaram. (b) Mahavira (Vardhamana Mahavira).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The ________ at Mount Abu is one of the most beautiful Jaina temples. (b) The Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at ________.
questions.answer: (a) Dilwara temple. (b) Kushinagar.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Mount Kailash, a sacred pilgrimage, lies in the south-west of the Tibetan region. (b) Amarnath caves are known as 'The Shrine Eternal'.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: Somnath is called the Shrine Eternal (Amarnath is the ice Shivling cave).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) 'Jai Badri Vishal' is the call of pilgrims visiting Badrinath, the home of Lord ________. (b) Rameshwaram is situated at the tip of the Indian ________.
questions.answer: (a) Vishnu. (b) Peninsula.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The only temple dedicated to Lord Brahma is situated in ________. (b) ________ temple is located in the mighty Trikuta Mountains.
questions.answer: (a) Pushkar. (b) Vaishno Devi.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Brajbhoomi is associated with God Ram. (b) Buddha gave his first sermon at Lumbini.
questions.answer: (a) False: with Lord Krishna. (b) False: at Sarnath.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The sacred place that was the capital of Sri Krishna's kingdom is ________. (b) The place where Sri Ram built a bridge over the sea to Sri Lanka is ________.
questions.answer: (a) Dwarka. (b) Rameshwaram.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The name of the Hindu goddess ________ means 'renowned goddess of desire'. (b) The place where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras attained moksha is ________.
questions.answer: (a) Kamakhya. (b) Mount Parsvanatha (Sametshikhar).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) A Buddhist religious centre at Sanchi was founded by ________. (b) Mahavira died at ________ at the age of 72.
questions.answer: (a) Ashoka. (b) Pawapuri.

questions.q: True or False. (a) The Rath Yatra is held at Puri. (b) Digambaras wear white clothes.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: Digambaras are sky-clad and Shwetambaras wear white.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Sringeri (b) Dwarka. B: (i) Jagat Mandir (ii) Goddess Sharada on the Tunga river (iii) Gundicha temple.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Describe any two points of significance of Kedarnath as a popular destination for Hindu pilgrims.
questions.answer: It is the remotest of the Char Dham sites, on the Mandakini river near the Chorabari glacier in the Himalayas. Its temple is one of the holiest Hindu temples and is named after King Kedar.

or.q: Describe any two points of significance of Nalanda as an important centre of Buddhists.
or.answer: It was an ancient seat of Buddhist learning from the 4th to 12th century with 2,000 teachers and 10,000 students. Hiuen Tsang studied there and praised its education.

questions.q: Describe the main sects of Jainism.
questions.answer: Jainism has two sects: the Digambaras (sky-clad, wear no clothes) and the Shwetambaras (wear white clothes).

or.q: Why is the Jain temple at Mount Abu in Rajasthan famous? Explain in two points.
or.answer: The Dilwara temples are masterpieces of Jain architecture built in white marble with delicate carving. They were built by Vimala Shah (about 1030) and Tejapala (about 1230).

questions.q: Describe any two characteristics of Udaygiri as a holy place for Buddhists.
questions.answer: It is a Buddhist site in Odisha dating from the 6th century. In the 8th century it was an important centre of Vajrayana art and philosophy.

questions.q: Describe the three main teachings of Lord Mahavira.
questions.answer: He preached non-violence (ahimsa), truth and non-possession and non-stealing as the four vows. He taught the threefold path of right belief, knowledge and conduct and equality of all people.

questions.q: Describe the sacred value of Mathura in any two points.
questions.answer: Mathura is the birthplace of Lord Krishna on the Yamuna and is known as Brajbhoomi. Holi and Janmashtami draw pilgrims and tourists to Mathura and Vrindavan.

questions.q: State the four vows taught by Mahavira.
questions.answer: Not to injure life, not to tell lies, not to own property and not to steal.

questions.q: What is the Eightfold Path of Buddhism?
questions.answer: It is the path of right view, resolution, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and meditation (conduct) that removes desire and leads to nirvana.

questions.q: Name the four mathas established by Adi Shankaracharya.
questions.answer: Badrinath in the north, Dwarka in the west, Puri in the east and Sringeri in the south.

questions.q: What is Rath Yatra? Where is it held?
questions.answer: It is the annual festival at Puri when the idols of Jagannath, Balram and Subhadra are taken in raths to the Gundicha temple and brought back after some days.

questions.q: Why is Bodh Gaya important for Buddhists?
questions.answer: Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree here, and it is one of the four most sacred Buddhist sites. The Mahabodhi Temple stands here.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three Jain heritage sites located in Rajasthan.
questions.answer: (i) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, built in white marble with fine carving. (ii) Ranakpur temple (15th century) with 1,444 carved pillars and four marble statues of Rishabha. (iii) Jaisalmer, with intricately carved yellow-stone temples and a famous library of Jain manuscripts.

questions.q: Explain the significance of Amarnath as a holy place of Hindus.
questions.answer: (i) It is a cave shrine of Lord Shiva in Jammu and Kashmir surrounded by snowy mountains. (ii) It is open to pilgrims only for a short period in summer. (iii) Lakhs of pilgrims make an annual trek to see the ice Shivling.

questions.q: Explain any three points of significance of Shravanabelagola as a holy place for Jains.
questions.answer: (i) It has the 57-ft monolithic statue of Bahubali carved about 980 CE, the biggest free-standing monolithic statue in the world. (ii) It stands on a hill reached by about five hundred steps. (iii) Every 12 to 15 years the Mahamastakabhisheka is held when the statue is showered from scaffolding.

questions.q: Describe the sacred value of Banaras (Varanasi) for Hindus in three points.
questions.answer: (i) It is the most sacred city, the city of Shiva, with over two thousand temples. (ii) It is on the Ganga and Hindus wish to die here to attain moksha. (iii) It was a great centre of learning, called the Athens of India by Bernier.

questions.q: Describe the religious heritage values of Dwarka, Puri and Somnath.
questions.answer: (i) Dwarka was the capital of Krishna's kingdom with Jagat Mandir. (ii) Puri has the Jagannath temple and the Rath Yatra. (iii) Somnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, known as the Shrine Eternal.

questions.q: Explain any three Buddhist heritage sites in India.
questions.answer: (i) Sarnath, where Buddha preached the first sermon, has the Dhamekh Stupa and Ashokan pillar. (ii) Bodh Gaya has the Mahabodhi Temple where he was enlightened. (iii) Sanchi's Great Stupa, founded by Ashoka, has fine toranas.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Write an essay on the life and teachings of Vardhamana Mahavira, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) He was the 24th Tirthankara, born at Vaishali to Siddhartha, a Kshatriya clan chief. (ii) At thirty he left home and meditated for twelve years until he became the Jina. (iii) He rejected belief in God, yagnas and the caste system and taught equality. (iv) He taught four vows: not to injure life, tell lies, own property or steal. (v) The threefold path of right belief, knowledge and conduct leads to moksha, and ahimsa is the central principle. (vi) He preached in Ardha Magadhi (Prakrit), Jainism later split into Digambaras and Shwetambaras and he died at Pawapuri at 72.

questions.q: Who was the founder of Buddhism? Explain the teachings of Buddha in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Gautama Buddha, born at Lumbini in 567 BCE, founded Buddhism. (ii) Seeing an old man, a sick man and a dead man, he left home and was enlightened at Bodh Gaya. (iii) He gave his first sermon at Sarnath. (iv) He taught that desire is the cause of suffering. (v) He taught the Eightfold Path of right view, resolution, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and meditation. (vi) He preached in Pali and Prakrit and stressed morality and virtue; the Sangha and viharas spread his teachings.

questions.q: Discuss Hindu religious heritage sites in India in six points.
questions.answer: (i) The four mathas and Dhams: Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri and Rameshwaram (and Sringeri). (ii) Varanasi, the city of Shiva and moksha. (iii) Haridwar, Prayag (Kumbh Mela) and Ayodhya. (iv) Mathura and Vrindavan, the land of Krishna. (v) Kedarnath, Amarnath, Somnath and Mount Kailash for Shiva. (vi) Vaishno Devi, Tirupati Balaji, Kamakhya and Pushkar.

questions.q: Discuss the major Jain heritage sites of India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Mount Parsvanatha in Bihar, where twenty Tirthankaras attained moksha. (ii) Pawapuri, where Mahavira attained nirvana. (iii) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu in white marble. (iv) Ranakpur with 1,444 carved pillars. (v) Girnar and Shatrunjaya in Gujarat. (vi) Shravanabelagola with the 57-ft Bahubali statue.
